Subject: E2E latency gating — procurement asks & next steps

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and the asks we promised. Short version: Veridian's p95 / p99 targets are aggressive given current traffic shape; we should align on traffic envelope, streaming concurrency expectations, and procurement milestones before the engineering POC.

Recap (from our side):
- Business targets: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms for the user-facing request path (includes our client-side post-processing).
- Current provider: Devon indicated 300ms p95 / ~800ms p99 for the same envelope during peak.
- Key constraints: streaming clients (long lived streams, ~20-30 tokens/sec), cold-start bursts (short windows with high concurrency), and KV-cache hit rates vary across endpoints.

Immediate asks (today):
1) Veridian to confirm a representative traffic envelope (time-of-day distribution, median and 95th request token lengths, percent streaming vs non-streaming).
2) Procurement (cc'd) to outline any SSO/SOW/contract prerequisites and a target procurement timeline.
3) Agree on a POC scope: we propose a 2-week POC that runs production-mirrored traffic at 10% sample for 72 hours + a focused synthetic tail-probing run.

Attachments: veridian_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (latency buckets & example traces), streaming-configs.json (expected streaming codec/settings).

Next steps from Redwood: we will provide an SLO gating checklist and a proposed canary schedule after we receive the traffic envelope.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Veridian to confirm a representative traffic envelope
We attached our traffic envelope export (see: traffic-envelope-Apr2027.csv) to this reply. Key bits: peak 11:30-12:30 PST, 18k rps aggregate, streaming sessions ~18% of requests, median request length 48 tokens, 95th token length 320.

> 2) Procurement prerequisites
Procurement: our timeline is internal sign-off by May 6th. We need an initial SOW and a standard security questionnaire response (we can accept your SOC 2 type II documentation and a short network diagram). Can you provide a draft SOW and the security artifact links?

> 3) POC scope
We are open to the 2-week approach. One ask: can Redwood do a focused p99 tail-probing mode (sustained low-rate tail traffic with synthetic long-calls) while we mirror production for the rest? That will help us understand the tail behavior independent of multi-tenant noise.

Forwarding the envelope now. Let us know if you want the raw Kafka topic samples — Devon can share on request.

Thanks Maya — good envelope and thanks for the procurement timeline. A few technical clarifications and what Redwood can commit for the POC: 

Quoted for context:
> We are open to the 2-week approach. One ask: can Redwood do a focused p99 tail-probing mode (sustained low-rate tail traffic with synthetic long-calls) while we mirror production for the rest?

Yes — that is exactly the kind of probing we recommend. Clarifications and proposed test plan: 
- Baseline run (mirrored traffic): 72 hours at ~10% sampling. We'll collect end-to-end traces (client timestamp, server recv, server send, token-stream milestones) and our internal queue/backpressure metrics.
- Tail-probing run: 6 hours of low-rate synthetic long-calls (we'll seed 500 concurrent long calls with 600-token sequences) to measure p99 under streaming and KV-cache miss conditions.
- Concurrency guidance: please expect that to achieve p95 <= 200ms under your envelope we'll need to provision at least ~1.3x current max concurrent stream slots compared to incumbent; we'll provide an exact tranche after an initial dry-run.
- Streaming settings: set keepalive to 90s and max concurrent streams per connection to 8 for the client SDK; Redwood will accept HTTP/2 streaming and gRPC if you prefer — we'll align on codec.
- Observability: we'll share a temporary Grafana dashboard and a zipped trace export (no raw customer content) for your engineers to inspect.

Attachments we will send after agreement: a short SLO gating checklist, the exact synthetic payloads for tail probing, and a draft SOW.

Proposed schedule:
- Apr 19: Redwood sends draft SOW + SLO checklist + probing payloads
- Apr 22: Baseline 72-hour mirrored run starts (10% sample)
- Apr 25: Tail-probing 6-hour window + analysis
- Apr 27: We deliver a short report with p95/p99 results and recommended capacity tranche.

Let us know if Procurement needs different dates; otherwise we will prepare the SOW and the security artifact links (SOC 2, network diagram) today.
